column1: # 2026-09-22-3f7c: the places in the GATED test assemblies where the clock is the SUBJECT,
# not the scaffolding — a stub that must take measurably longer than its siblings, a limit
# that must be elapsed past, a timestamp that must move. Every one of them is a LOWER bound
# or a stub's own behaviour, so a slower host satisfies it more easily rather than less.
# Everywhere else a test says WHAT it waits for and never HOW LONG: TestWaits carries the
# suite's one hang ceiling, and no assertion may carry a deadline of its own. A new entry
# here is a claim that the clock is the subject — make that claim in review, not in passing.

column3: why the clock is the subject
a stub child that finishes after its siblings, so the merge order cannot be the completion order
a stub limiter whose wait IS the quantity the ledger reports upward
elapsing past a zero-second limit, which is the limit being enforced
a call that must measurably last, and two calls that must order by start time
a call that outlives a zero-second wall-clock limit
the operator cancel the transport must map to a null answer
a change timestamp that must move, and one that must not
the poll cadence of a wait already budgeted on STALL rather than on total time
an operator cancel against a long child, and a duration held against that child's own sleep
